ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Approximately 75% low-intensity (black/dark-grey) coverage vs 25% high-intensity (white/light-grey) streaks and focal points.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous dark-intensity region occupying the central and lower fluke area. High-intensity pixels are distributed as linear streaks across the center of both lobes and concentrated as dense mottled clusters near the upper trailing edges and distal tips.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, narrow V-shaped notch with an approximate angle of 45 degrees; vertical depth occupies significant pixel space relative to the lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: The left lobe exhibits fine, low-amplitude serrations. The right lobe trailing edge is characterized by high-amplitude, irregular indentations and jagged pixel-boundaries, particularly near the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Leading edges maintain a smooth convex curve. The trailing edge of the left lobe follows a standard concave sweep, while the right lobe trajectory is interrupted by multiple irregular concave depressions.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense, high-contrast, textured clusters of light-brown and white pixels located at the distal apex of both lobes, consistent with barnacle colonization.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Significant presence of multi-directional white linear pixel-paths (rake marks) cutting across the dark-intensity ventral surface, primarily visible on the inner right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive irregular tissue loss and raggedness along the trailing edge of the right lobe, indicating significant physical trauma; numerous intersecting linear scar patterns across the central fluke surface.
other_distinctive_markers: A prominent, bulbous, three-dimensional textured mass is visible at the extreme upper tip of the right lobe, distinct from the flat pigmentation of the fluke body.
